subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any authenticated or pre-auth Gateway request path copy attacker-controlled `params` keys into a prototype-sensitive target, making this report exploitable rather than parser-only hardening?
rationale: Current source disproves the report's stated Zod and command-parser premise, but `params` remains method-defined and a complete security verdict depends on owner review of core, plugin, and auxiliary handler sinks.

options.title: Audit then close
options.body: Confirm no reachable handler performs an unsafe merge or dynamic assignment, record the reviewed sink classes, and close as not exploitable.

options.title: Patch the proven sink
options.body: If a reachable sink exists, harden that owner boundary and add a regression test using `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` payloads.

options.title: Adopt parser-wide rejection
options.body: Reject prototype-named keys globally only after confirming that the protocol compatibility cost is intentional and all arbitrary-JSON RPC contracts remain supported.

recommendation.title: Audit then close
recommendation.body: Confirm no reachable handler performs an unsafe merge or dynamic assignment, record the reviewed sink classes, and close as not exploitable.

likelyOwner.reason: This team owns the relevant security boundaries in CODEOWNERS and is best placed to decide exploitability and acceptable protocol hardening.
